title: Minimum Uncovered Sum with Dominoes
statement:
You are given an `N x N` grid of non-negative integers and a number `K`. You have `K` rectangular slabs, each of which covers exactly **two adjacent cells** (two cells that share a side, either horizontally or vertically).

Place **at most `K` slabs** on the grid so that no cell is covered by more than one slab and every slab lies fully inside the grid. Your goal is to **minimise the sum of the values of the uncovered cells**.

Print that minimum sum. (Because all values are non-negative, covering more cells never hurts, so you only place fewer than `K` slabs when no further slab fits.)
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `N` and `K`.
Each of the next `N` lines contains `N` space-separated integers: the rows of the grid.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the minimum possible sum of uncovered cells.

examples.explanation: With one slab the best placement covers the bottom row (8 and 7). The uncovered cells are 6 and 4, so the sum is 10.
The total is 29. Cover the two 9s with one slab (18) and the 5 with an adjacent 1 (6): 24 is covered, leaving 5. No two slabs can cover more than 9 + 9 + 5 + 1 = 24.
A 1 x 1 grid has no room for any slab, so the single cell stays uncovered.

hints: Maximise the covered sum instead: answer = total of all cells minus the best sum covered by at most K non-overlapping slabs.

A slab overlaps at most 6 other slabs (each of its two cells belongs to at most 3 others). So in an optimal solution it is enough to consider the 6K heaviest slab positions: if the solution used a slab outside that set, one of the 6K candidates is free of conflicts and at least as heavy.

Pick the 6K heaviest positions (by sum of the two cells) and run a small DFS/branch-and-bound over them, choosing at most K that do not share a cell. Stop a branch when even the heaviest remaining slabs cannot beat the best answer so far.
